findings.issue: P123-R3 is closed only at the runner, and its consequence (phases kept provisional, release held) is still reachable. _run_full now records a row built from the filtered commands (`_record_full_run(..., commands, ...)`, published = filtered list). Every reader of that row builds `declared` from the unfiltered `_ev.resolved_commands(manifest, meta.fullGate)`, review-only value included. (a) For a mixed fullGate [ok, claimsMatchCode], the green row has one step against two declared entries, so `_full_disqualification` answers 'FULL RUN RAN 1 OF 2 DECLARED ENTRIES'. The run is never whole-bearing, every merged phase stays PROVISIONAL and guard-release holds the release. (b) For a fullGate holding only review-only entries, run-test-gate returns E_ASK (= 2). full-gate.py's `declares_full_gate` still says a third place is declared, and its docstring (':133 THE SAME PRESENCE CHECK run-test-gate's own _run_full makes') is now false. So the pre-push/CI step prints 'the run is still red - exit 2 blocks the push', and the readers wait for a full run nothing can record. fo2 (plugins/audit/tests/test_run_test_gate.py:8640) asserts only the exit code and the step list. It never asks `_ev.full_status` / `_full_disqualification` about the row it pins, and no case drives full-gate.py over either plan.
findings.resolution: Put one declared-full-gate list in _evidence_io: `resolved_commands` drops review-only values, or a new `full_gate_commands(manifest)` does. Make run-test-gate._run_full, full-gate.declares_full_gate, every full_status caller (audit-status, render-report, _doctor_trail, _panel_composition) and guard-release read that one list, so a fullGate holding only review-only entries reads as 'no third place' (NOT_DECLARED, exit 0) everywhere. Extend fo2 to assert `_ev._full_disqualification(row, declared)` is None for the recorded row, and add a test_full_gate case for the review-only-only plan exiting 0.

findings.issue: split_not_commands classifies the RESOLVED command, and `resolved_commands` has already prefixed `meta.nodePreamble` to it ('<lead> && review-only: ...'). `is_review_only` only accepts a value that begins with 'review-only:', so in any plan that sets nodePreamble a review-only entry is not split out. Its prose then runs through the shell on the task/phase path (:4821) and on the full path this phase added (:4502), and records a red gate: the defect P123.49 and P123.55 exist to stop. No case pairs nodePreamble with a review-only entry (test_run_test_gate.py names nodePreamble only in the rg1b resolution cases).
findings.resolution: Classify each entry by its raw buildCommands value (or the entry itself) before the preamble is joined. For example, have split_not_commands take the entries and meta.buildCommands, or have resolved_commands return the review-only flag beside each pair. Add a case with nodePreamble set and a review-only entry in testGate and in fullGate, asserting no step ran.

findings.issue: P123-R7 is partly open. There is now one reader, but the two hooks still call it with different seams. guard-secrets-read passes the disk `is_dir` and `files_of`. guard-bash-writes calls `_config.copy_destinations(words)` with neither. So `cp a.py src` (src an existing directory) is graded as src/a.py by the plan gate and attributed as `src` by guard-bash-writes, and `cp -r dir dest` / `mv dir dest` are listed per file by one and named as one word by the other. That is exactly the 'no is_dir reading' disagreement R7 named. In guard-bash-writes the mismatch moves a path from `named` to `unproven`, so with another session active (clauses) the deny tier only gives a notice where it would block. The new docstring's 'so one command gets one answer' (_config.py:2275) is false at runtime. ww7c compares `M._copy_destinations(w)` (now `_config.copy_destinations(w) or []`) against `_config.copy_destinations(w) or []`: the same function, with no seam on either side and only spellings that do not need the disk. It cannot see this disagreement.
findings.resolution: Have guard-bash-writes pass the same seams: an is_dir and files_of resolved at the command's cwd, ideally built by one helper in _config that both hooks call. Rewrite ww7c to drive both hooks' own call paths over a fixture holding an existing slashless directory and a recursive copy, and assert they agree.

findings.issue: The layer-number class P123.33 promised to close ('Every layer number written in prose is checked against _deps.LAYERS or not written') is still open one wording over. R2 widened the regex to the shapes the finding listed. But present-tense mentions in the 'at LN' / 'is at layer N' / '(now LN' / 'sits at layer N' wordings are not read, and many are the same off-by-one. Examples: '`_refs` is at layer 1' (LAYERS index 2), '`_manifest_ado` at L2 grades the config' (3), '`_help` (now L2)' (3, while _deps.py:214 says L3 and passes), '`_panel_state` sits at layer 5' (6). A read-only probe that widened `_NAMED_LAYER_MENTION` to those connectives over `_real_source_files`/`_prose_blocks` matched dozens of disagreements with LAYERS. A few are history ('sat at', 'came down to'); most are present tense. This is a second round on one class, so enumerating more wordings will not close it.
findings.resolution: Grade by invariant, not by wording: for every prose block, any `L<n>` / `layer <n>` within the same sentence as a backticked LAYERS name is checked, with an explicit history exemption ('sat at', 'moved', 'came down', 'used to'). Or delete the numbers where the layer is not the argument, as the R2 resolution asked. Add an lmd case and a prove-gates row for the 'at LN' shape.

findings.issue: layer_mention_drift's docstring still says it 'reads the three shapes it can read reliably' after P123.54 widened `_NAMED_LAYER_MENTION` to the qualified, comma and unclosed forms. The comment above the regex was updated and the function's docstring was not.
findings.resolution: Drop the count ('reads the shapes `_NAMED_LAYER_MENTION` and `_OWN_LAYER_MENTION` name').

findings.issue: P123.60's task text asks for the regression 'a triage over a finding whose issue holds a backtick span with a spaced paren adds its fix task'. The diff relies on fb1, whose finding carries ' :400' and no backtick span. The stdin batch makes the shape irrelevant to argv, so the risk is low, but the named regression is not pinned.
findings.resolution: Give COLON_FINDINGS' second issue the literal shape that stopped the P123 triage (e.g. 'see `(split_not_commands at :4809)`'), so fb1 covers it.

findings.issue: Unrelated existing lines were rewritten to `before =open(...)`, `gate =(...)` and `CE_TEST ="tests/test_a.py"`. These are stray whitespace edits (E225) that ruff's selected rules do not catch, and the same artefact appears in two separate task commits, which points at an editing tool rather than intent.
findings.resolution: Restore `X = Y` on those lines, and find what rewrote them before it touches non-test code.
